quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #7
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When backing up, what should you do?

options.text: Look through the rear window.
Press hard on the gas pedal.
Rely only on your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look through the rear window.
questions.explanation: When backing up, place your right arm on the back of the passenger seat and look through the rear window. Mirrors do not show what is directly behind your vehicle. Always drive in reverse slowly.

questions.question: What must you do at a flashing yellow light?

options.text: Come to a complete stop at the intersection.
Maintain your normal speed.
Slow down and proceed with caution.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed with caution.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light tells you to be alert and proceed carefully. Slow down when you see a flashing yellow light.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Road widens ahead.
Lane reduction. The right lane ends soon and traffic should merge left.
Highway entrance ramp ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lane reduction. The right lane ends soon and traffic should merge left.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns that lanes ahead will be reduced and traffic must merge to the left.

questions.question: What should you do at a traffic light that is not working?

options.text: Come to a full stop and yield the right-of-way before entering the intersection.
If the intersection is clear, you do not need to stop.
Drive quickly through the intersection to get out of the way of other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a full stop and yield the right-of-way before entering the intersection.
questions.explanation: When a traffic light is not working, treat the intersection as an all-way stop. Come to a complete stop. Look both ways and yield the right-of-way before entering the intersection.

questions.question: What does a solid yellow line on your side of the centerline mean?

options.text: Reduce your speed.
Traffic light ahead.
Do not pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not pass.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow line on your side means you cannot pass. On two-lane roads, solid yellow lines mark areas where passing is not safe from that direction.

questions.question: When must you use your low beam headlights?

options.text: On a lighted street.
On a freeway.
In fog.

questions.correctAnswerText: In fog.
questions.explanation: Use low beams when driving in fog, snow, rain, or mist. High beams reflect off these conditions and create glare that makes it harder to see. Fog lights can also help.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Drive with caution and be ready to stop.
You must come to a complete stop.
Stop, if necessary.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: A stop sign is the only eight-sided sign on the road. You must come to a complete stop. Do not proceed until the way is clear and you can safely pass through the intersection.

questions.question: What should you do when driving in fog?

options.text: Turn on your high beam headlights.
Slow down and use your low beam headlights.
Increase your speed so you do not cause an accident.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and use your low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: In fog, slow down and use low beam lights. If fog is too thick to see, pull off the road and wait for it to clear.

questions.question: When must vehicles stop behind a school bus with red lights flashing?

options.text: All students are off the bus.
The stop arm is retracted.
The stop arm is retracted and the bus resumes motion.

questions.correctAnswerText: The stop arm is retracted and the bus resumes motion.
questions.explanation: When a school bus has red lights flashing and its stop arm extended, you must stay stopped until the lights turn off, the stop arm is pulled back, and the bus starts moving again.

questions.question: Which statement about blind spots is true?

options.text: Blind spots are eliminated if you have one outside mirror.
Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most passenger vehicles.
Blind spots can be checked by looking in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most passenger vehicles.
questions.explanation: All vehicles have blind spots that mirrors cannot show. Large trucks have much larger blind spots than regular cars.

questions.question: When driving at night, you should:

options.text: Always use your high beams.
Look directly at the headlights of an oncoming vehicle.
Increase your following distance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase your following distance.
questions.explanation: When it is dark and hard to see, increase the distance between you and the car ahead. Use your headlights properly. Do not look directly at oncoming headlights because the bright light can blind you.

questions.question: Excessive speed:

options.text: Does not increase the chance of a crash.
Increases your ability to react to a hazard.
Often leads to high-risk decision-making.

questions.correctAnswerText: Often leads to high-risk decision-making.
questions.explanation: Excessive speed is a major cause of crashes. Driving too fast does not save time and often leads to dangerous decisions.

questions.question: You are driving on a one-way street. You may only turn left onto another one-way street if:

options.text: You increase your speed before the turn.
Traffic on the street moves to the right.
Traffic on the street moves to the left.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic on the street moves to the left.
questions.explanation: You can turn left onto a one-way street if traffic on that street moves to the left and there is no sign that prohibits the turn. You cannot turn left onto a one-way street where traffic moves to the right.

questions.question: If a tire blows out, you should:

options.text: Apply the brake and hold it.
Hold the steering wheel tightly and use the brakes lightly.
Pull over quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the steering wheel tightly and use the brakes lightly.
questions.explanation: If a tire blows out, grip the steering wheel tightly and keep the vehicle straight. Slow down gradually by easing off the gas and braking gently. Move off the road to a safe place when you can.

questions.question: When entering traffic after being parked at a curb, you:

options.text: Should drive more slowly than other traffic for 200 feet.
Should wait for a large enough gap to get up to the speed of traffic.
Should wait for the first two vehicles to pass, then drive into the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should wait for a large enough gap to get up to the speed of traffic.
questions.explanation: When merging into traffic in the city or on a highway, wait for enough space to speed up and match the speed of other vehicles.

questions.question: This sign is a:

options.text: Yield sign.
School crossing sign.
Stop sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield sign.
questions.explanation: A triangle pointing down is always a yield sign. When you see a yield sign, be ready to slow down or stop.

questions.question: When you see an emergency vehicle approaching while using its flashing lights, you must:

options.text: Maintain your speed and stay in your lane until the vehicle has passed.
Move into the right lane and drive slowly until the vehicle has passed.
Pull over to the curb or edge of the road and stop until the vehicle has passed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over to the curb or edge of the road and stop until the vehicle has passed.
questions.explanation: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights coming, move to the right edge of the road and stop. Pull parallel to the curb. On one-way streets, move to the nearest edge of the road.

questions.question: When should drivers use hand-over-hand steering?

options.text: When turning the wheel during normal driving activity.
When backing or when momentarily turning on blinkers, the radio, or windshield wipers.
When turning the wheel at low speeds to make a sharp turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: When turning the wheel at low speeds to make a sharp turn.
questions.explanation: Use hand-over-hand steering when making a sharp turn at low speed. When the turn is complete, straighten the wheel using your hands.

questions.question: You should allow an extra cushion of space:

options.text: When following a station wagon.
When following a driver who cannot see the rear of their vehicle.
When following a small passenger car.

questions.correctAnswerText: When following a driver who cannot see the rear of their vehicle.
questions.explanation: Drivers of trucks, buses, vans, and vehicles with trailers or campers may not see you directly behind them. Stay farther back from these vehicles. Large vehicles also block your view of the road ahead, so increase your distance to see around them.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a safe driving practice when driving on the interstate?

options.text: Slower traffic must keep to the right.
Change lanes without signaling.
If you miss your exit, you must go to the next exit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes without signaling.
questions.explanation: Always signal when changing lanes. On the interstate, keep right if you are driving slower than other traffic. You cannot back up or make a U-turn on the interstate, so go to the next exit if you miss yours.

questions.question: What should a driver do?

options.text: Assume all drivers follow right-of-way rules.
Assume most drivers follow right-of-way rules.
Always be ready to give up the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always be ready to give up the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: Right-of-way rules guide who should yield, but do not assume you automatically have the right-of-way. Always think about what is happening at the intersection. Yield your right-of-way if it helps prevent a crash.

questions.question: You are parking downhill on a two-way road with no curb. Which way should you turn your front wheels?

options.text: Straight ahead
Right, toward the edge of the road
Left, toward the center of the road

questions.correctAnswerText: Right, toward the edge of the road
questions.explanation: When parking downhill (with or without a curb), or uphill without a curb, turn your wheels toward the road edge. This way, your car rolls away from traffic if the brakes fail. When parking uphill with a curb, turn wheels toward the center so your car rolls into the curb if brakes fail.

questions.question: When changing lanes, how can you check your blind spot?

options.text: Use the inside rearview mirror.
Turn your head and look over your shoulder.
Use your side mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Mirrors cannot show blind spots. Before changing lanes, look over your shoulder to see these hidden areas.

questions.question: How can you help avoid skidding on slippery surfaces?

options.text: Shift to a lower gear after starting down a steep hill.
Speed up to enter curves and slow down to exit them.
Slow down before entering curves and intersections.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down before entering curves and intersections.
questions.explanation: Slow down before entering a curve because you cannot see what is ahead. Braking while turning can cause you to skid.

questions.question: When should you check your rearview mirrors?

options.text: Often to see how traffic is moving behind you.
To see if a vehicle is in your blind spot.
Only when you are slowing down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Often to see how traffic is moving behind you.
questions.explanation: Do not stare in one direction. Check your rearview mirrors often so you know where vehicles are around you.
